members: Tertiary amine TCAs include clomipramine, amitriptyline, imipramine, and doxepin; secondary amine TCAs include desipramine and nortriptyline (Dulcan p.754)
MAOIs include phenelzine, isocarboxazid, tranylcypromine, and selegiline (Dulcan p.754)
drug_class.mechanism: TCAs inhibit SERT and NET, and block H1, M1, alpha1, and voltage-sensitive sodium channels (StahlNeuro p.335). MAOIs irreversibly inhibit MAO-A and MAO-B (StahlNeuro p.339).
kinetics: Clomipramine is metabolized extensively to the active noradrenergic metabolite desmethyl-clomipramine (de-CMI) by CYP450 1A2 (StahlKids p.135)
CYP450 2D6 inhibitors like fluoxetine and paroxetine can significantly increase clomipramine plasma concentrations (StahlKids p.130)
MAOIs are irreversible enzyme inhibitors requiring weeks for new enzyme synthesis (StahlNeuro p.338)
drug_class.onset_of_effect: Conventional antidepressants take weeks of oral administration to achieve a clinical response (Dulcan p.754)

items: Clomipramine is FDA-approved for pediatric OCD (StahlKids p.125)
Imipramine is used for short-term treatment of childhood enuresis (Dulcan p.459)
Amitriptyline and imipramine can be used off-label for encopresis (Dulcan p.468)
Selegiline transdermal patch is used off-label for adolescent MDD (Dulcan p.754)
key_numbers: 10 years: Minimum age approved by the FDA for clomipramine in pediatric OCD (StahlKids p.125)
5 years: Minimum developmental age required for a diagnosis of enuresis (DSM p.400)
2 times per week: Minimum frequency of enuresis required for diagnosis (DSM p.400)
3 months: Minimum duration of symptoms required for enuresis diagnosis (DSM p.400)

items: TCA side effects include anticholinergic effects, sedation, orthostatic hypotension, and cardiotoxicity (StahlNeuro p.335)
TCAs lower the seizure threshold in susceptible patients (StahlKids p.133)
Antidepressant treatment can induce Treatment-Emergent Activation Syndrome (TEAS) in pediatric patients (StahlKids p.126)
MAOIs can cause fatal hypertensive crises or serotonin syndrome if combined with contraindicated agents (StahlNeuro p.338)
key_numbers: 250 mg/day: Dosing limit for clomipramine above which seizure risk increases significantly (StahlKids p.135)
440 ms: QTc interval threshold in children; exceeding it increases Torsades de Pointes risk (Dulcan p.332)
12 years: Age under which children are more susceptible to TCA cardiotoxicity due to rapid metabolism to desmethyl forms (Dulcan p.754)

items: Baseline ECG is mandatory before starting a TCA to rule out congenitally prolonged QTc or arrhythmias, with repeat ECGs after dose titrations (Dulcan p.332)
Regular face-to-face monitoring is recommended during the first several weeks of treatment to assess for suicidal ideation (StahlKids p.442)
Correct hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia before or during treatment to prevent worsening of QTc prolongation (Dulcan p.832)
Weigh patients and track height against normal growth trajectories due to TCA-associated weight gain (StahlKids p.125, p.442)
key_numbers: 500 ms: QTc interval threshold at which a TCA must be discontinued (Dulcan p.832)
2 weeks: Time period required to titrate clomipramine from 25 mg/day to the initial target of 100 mg/day (StahlKids p.128)

items: Titrate TCA doses slowly with meals to minimize GI side effects, and give at bedtime to reduce daytime sedation (StahlKids p.128)
Obtain informed consent from both legal guardians for drug therapy, regardless of custody percentages (StahlKids p.137)
Children often have shorter half-lives and duration of action due to rapid liver metabolism, requiring more frequent dosing (StahlKids p.11, p.135)
key_numbers: 25 mg/day: Standard starting dose of clomipramine for pediatric patients (StahlKids p.128)
100 mg/day: Standard target dose of clomipramine after 2 weeks of titration (StahlKids p.128)
7 years: Minimum age for which lithium is FDA-approved to treat acute manic or mixed states (Dulcan p.764)

items: TCAs have a narrow therapeutic index and represent a high risk of lethality in overdose (Dulcan p.332)
TCA overdose blocks voltage-sensitive sodium channels in the brain and heart, causing coma, seizures, arrhythmias, and death (StahlNeuro p.338)
key_numbers: 1 in 3000: Estimated proportion of antidepressant prescriptions that are MAOIs, reflecting their rare use due to lethality and dietary restrictions (StahlNeuro p.338)

items: MAOIs require strict dietary restrictions to avoid tyramine-induced hypertensive crises (StahlNeuro p.338)
Selegiline transdermal patch was judged safe and tolerated in adolescents, although efficacy was not statistically superior to placebo (Dulcan p.754)
Washout periods of 2 weeks are mandatory when switching between MAOIs and other antidepressants to avoid serotonin syndrome (Dulcan p.744)
A 5-week washout is mandatory when switching from fluoxetine to an MAOI due to the long half-life of norfluoxetine (Dulcan p.737)
key_numbers: 14 days: Mandatory washout period required when transitioning between MAOIs and other antidepressants (Dulcan p.744)
5 weeks: Washout period required after stopping fluoxetine before starting an MAOI (Dulcan p.737)

high_yield: TCAs are not more effective than placebo for major depressive disorder in children and adolescents, and are not indicated for pediatric depression (Dulcan p.754)
Clomipramine is the sole TCA approved by the FDA for pediatric OCD (StahlKids p.125)
TCA cardiotoxicity is mediated by blockade of cardiac voltage-sensitive sodium channels, causing QRS and QTc prolongation (StahlNeuro p.338)
Co-administering fluvoxamine with clomipramine blocks its CYP1A2-mediated conversion, powerfully boosting its serotonergic profile in treatment-resistant OCD (StahlKids p.135)
A 5-week washout period is mandatory when switching from fluoxetine to an MAOI to prevent fatal serotonin syndrome (Dulcan p.737)
